statement: You are given a binary tree. The tree is given as the array tree in level order, indexed from 0: the root is tree[0], and the left and right children of the node at index i are at indices 2i + 1 and 2i + 2. null marks a position with no node, and every position below a null must be null too.
Standing to the right of the tree, you see the rightmost node of each level. Standing to the left, you see the leftmost node of each level.
Compute both views, each listed from the root's level downwards: rightView holds the right view and leftView holds the left view.

examples.explanation: 2 has only a right child 5, and 3 has only a right child 4. On the bottom level, 4 is further right than 5.
This is the same tree seen from the left. 5 is the leftmost node of the bottom level, even though it is a right child.
The tree is a chain of left children. Each level has one node, which is seen from either side.
